newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OPTIONS -- EOE calls in demand as index breaks 600.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -- EOE calls in demand as index breaks 600.

text.p: Trade pushed ahead on the European Options Exchange on Wednesday as market makers bought calls in the EOE contract as the underlying AEX index broke above the key 600 point barrier for the first time.

Option-related selling had weighed on shares but forced driving the AEX were too strong, outweighing the pressure from market makers who were forced to take out extra protection this afternoon ahead of the expiry on Friday.
But dealers said many were holding off until after the Fed meeting this evening which is expected not to recommend a rate rise, particularly after benign inflation data on Wednesday.
"There a lot of interest being generated by the index at this level but we'll have to wait until tomorrow to see how it breaks," one dealer said.
Inaction on the part of the FOMC was seen as most beneficial for the index and one dealer said the resultant short-covering by market makers could push the index ahead substantially.
A decision from the meeting is expected around 1915 GMT.

Well traded individual options included those in retailer Ahold, which clocked up more than 11,000 transactions as private investors learnt of a presentation to analysts in the U.S. scheduled later today. -- Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
